clue.text: At Cenotaph, bishop represented king giving tribute

indicators.note: something represented is presented again in another form, so the letters are set out anew

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: At a war memorial, a bishop speaks on behalf of the monarch while paying tribute.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop and king join the Cenotaph letters before the whole lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A pat on the back is an idiom for praise or congratulation, a small tribute to someone's work.

clue.text: Bill is in Penny Lane meeting comedian

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for a penny
La is the street-sign abbreviation for Lane
a card is a joker, an amusing person

explanation.surface: A poster turns up on Penny Lane, the Beatles' Liverpool street, alongside a comic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny Lane' reads as the Beatles song and street, but each word gives its own abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a printed notice posted up in public, which is exactly what a placard is.

clue.text: Schubert piano quintet rehearsal omits last bit of harmony

indicators.note: to omit something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped from the rehearsal word

parts.note: a tryout is a trial run or rehearsal

indicators.note: last points to the final position, the closing letter of the word

parts.note: the closing letter of harmony

explanation.surface: A run-through of a famous Schubert work drops the final touch of harmony.
explanation.walkthrough: TRYOUT loses its Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Schubert's Piano Quintet in A major is universally known by its nickname, the Trout Quintet, after the song it varies.

clue.text: Disreputable number associated with riotous cavorting

parts.note: No. is the abbreviation for number

indicators.note: cavorting means leaping about wildly, so the letters jump into new places

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A shady act is linked with wild, rowdy capering.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious means well known for something bad, which is a synonym of disreputable.

clue.text: Sacred tree — only one left

indicators.note: only one of a pair of the letter for left remains, so its twin is dropped

parts.note: holly is an evergreen tree

explanation.surface: A sacred tree stands alone, the only one remaining.
explanation.walkthrough: L is left; HOLLY has two of them and keeps only one.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy and sacred are synonyms, both meaning dedicated to God or a religious purpose.

clue.text: Bug found by advisory group brought up by incompetent under-secretary

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up turns it to read from bottom to top

parts.note: CAB is the Citizens Advice Bureau, a British free advice service
ill can mean badly or unskilfully done
US is the abbreviation for under-secretary

explanation.surface: An infection is traced to a government committee lifted by a hopeless junior minister.
explanation.walkthrough: The Citizens Advice Bureau, CAB, is a British charity giving free advice; written upwards it opens the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bacillus is a rod-shaped bacterium, and bug is the informal word for such a germ.

clue.text: Two forms of short shivery painful condition

indicators.note: something short is cut off before its end, so each word loses its final letter

parts.note: first form: feeling cold makes one shivery
second form: icy is another word for shivery

explanation.surface: A shivering fit comes in two kinds, both brief and painful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two forms of' means two synonyms of shivery, COLD and ICY, each docked by 'short'.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is severe abdominal pain, especially in babies, so it is a painful condition.

clue.text: Fuss when heartless youth disrupts dance spectacles?

indicators.note: to disrupt is to break into something, so one piece sits inside the others

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: without a heart means all the inner letters go, keeping only the ends

parts.note: the outside letters of youth
two round lenses look like a pair of letter Os

explanation.surface: A rowdy youngster spoils the show at a dance and causes a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spectacles' with its question mark is a picture clue: a pair of glasses looks like two round letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballyhoo is noisy commotion or extravagant publicity, which is a fuss.

clue.text: Pay, say, raised to get cheap jewellery

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a wage is pay
e.g. means for example, which say also means

explanation.surface: Wages are raised so that someone can buy trinkets.
explanation.definitionFit: A geegaw, or gewgaw, is a showy trinket of little value, so cheap jewellery fits.

clue.text: Papal internet provider accepts position in charge

indicators.note: to accept is to take something in, so one piece goes inside the provider

parts.note: AOL is a well-known internet service provider
a post is a job or position
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A web company with the Pope's business takes on a job in management.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pope's see is the Apostolic See, so apostolic is used to mean of or relating to the Pope.

clue.text: Will break sanction

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to bequeath, as in a will
second meaning: time off work, a holiday

explanation.surface: Someone is determined to defy a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings, not two: each of the three words defines the answer on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave is a verb for handing on by testament, a noun for a holiday from work, and a noun for permission granted.

clue.text: Main way bohemian embraces old queen

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: arty describes an artistic, bohemian type
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: An artistic free spirit hugs an elderly queen on the high street.
explanation.definitionFit: An artery is a main road or route, so a main way is a fair synonym for it.

clue.text: Traitor has malignant side

parts.note: black means evil or malign
the leg side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A betrayer is shown to have a wicked streak.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field divides into the off side and the leg side, so side gives the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackleg is a strikebreaker who works on during a strike, seen by fellow workers as a traitor.

clue.text: I'm obliged to pay newcomer returning moonshine

definitions.note: a statement the answer would make, standing for the person who owes

parts.note: a deb, or debutante, is a young woman newly entering society

indicators.note: something returning comes back the way it went, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: moonshine means nonsense, as does rot

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they must pay back a recent arrival for illicit liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: Moonshine looks like bootleg whisky here but means foolish talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A debtor is the person who owes money, so the words in their mouth would be that they must pay.

clue.text: Nerve of philosopher defending court edict originally

indicators.note: to defend is to surround and protect, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: Francis Bacon, the English philosopher
KB is King's Bench, an English court

indicators.note: originally points to the very start of the word, its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of edict

explanation.surface: A thinker shows courage by upholding the first ruling of a court.
explanation.walkthrough: King's Bench is a division of the English High Court; the philosopher is Francis Bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: Backbone figuratively means courage or strength of character, so nerve is a synonym.

clue.text: Pantomime elephant entertains quiet wife

indicators.note: to entertain is to host guests inside one's home, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Dumbo is Disney's flying elephant
sh is the call for quiet
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: In a pantomime, a pantomime elephant puts on a show for a silent wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pantomime' looks like the setting for the elephant but is the definition, in its older sense of a mimed show.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumbshow is a performance in gesture without words, which is what pantomime in its original sense means.

clue.text: Music produced by crude whistle-blower?

parts.note: blue means smutty or crude
a grass is British slang for an informer

explanation.surface: Tunes are made by a rough sort of whistler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistle-blower' suggests someone playing a whistle, fitting music, but means an informer, which British slang calls a grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluegrass is a style of American country music played on banjo, fiddle and guitar.

clue.text: Beginning to postpone changing hands

indicators.note: hands here means right and left, so one hand's letter is swapped for the other's

parts.note: to prorogue is to discontinue or defer a parliament's session

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to delay a sale of property.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) becomes L (left) in PROROGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A prologue is the introductory section of a play or book, its beginning.

clue.text: Turns up with Ultravox singer swaggering

parts.note: to cock is to turn up, as a hat brim or an ear
Midge Ure was the singer of the band Ultravox

explanation.surface: An eighties pop frontman arrives with a strut.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocksure means arrogantly over-confident, which shows itself in a swaggering manner.

clue.text: Supporters of Chapter Masses

parts.note: c is the abbreviation for chapter
a ruck is a crowd or mass

explanation.surface: Followers of a cathedral chapter attend services.
explanation.walkthrough: Masses looks like church services, fitting Chapter, but means crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: Crucks are pairs of curved timbers that hold up the roof of a building, so they are structural supports.

clue.text: Transatlantic partners recalled including note in puzzle

indicators.note: to include is to take inside, so a piece goes in the middle
something recalled is called back, so the pair is read in the backward direction

parts.note: Britain and America are allies either side of the Atlantic
do is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Allies across the ocean are summoned back over a message inside a brainteaser.
explanation.walkthrough: The note goes into the middle of the reversed pair, between its two country codes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudoku is a number-placement puzzle on a nine-by-nine grid.

clue.text: Bermudan heading off flying without weapons

indicators.note: flying letters are sent scattering, landing in a new order
with its heading off, the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller from Bermuda flies off without any weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Unarmed means carrying no arms, that is, having no weapons.

clue.text: Release foreign articles about Rogers?

indicators.note: about means around, so the articles go round a middle piece

parts.note: un and le are French articles
Buck Rogers is the science-fiction comic hero

explanation.surface: Free some imported goods concerning a man called Rogers.
explanation.walkthrough: UN and LE go either side of BUCK.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbuckle is to undo a buckle and so free or release what it was holding.

clue.text: Friend coming from march in Aldershot

indicators.note: coming from means emerging out of the following words, which contain the letters

parts.note: inside the words march in Aldershot

explanation.surface: A comrade turns up from a parade in Aldershot, the army garrison town.
explanation.walkthrough: Aldershot is the home of the British Army, which suits the march. 'China plate' is Cockney rhyming slang for mate.
explanation.definitionFit: China, short for china plate, rhymes with mate, so in Cockney slang it means a friend.

clue.text: Vehicle leaving Nicaragua crashed into animal

indicators.note: a crash leaves things smashed and jumbled into disorder
something leaving goes away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A car leaving Nicaragua hits a creature on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: An iguana is a large tropical lizard, an example of an animal, at home in Central America.

clue.text: Posh English operatic princess retracted valediction

indicators.note: retracted means drawn back, so the string runs backwards up the column

parts.note: U means upper-class
E is the abbreviation for English
Princess Ida is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera

explanation.surface: A smart English opera heroine withdraws her farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operatic princess' tempts AIDA, but the princess is Gilbert and Sullivan's Ida.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a French-derived word of farewell, and a valediction is a farewell.

clue.text: Galleon oddly in gorge

indicators.note: oddly means taking the odd-numbered positions, first, third and so on

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A sailing ship strangely finds itself in a ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland, so it is close in sense to a gorge.

clue.text: Foreign characters involved in Balkan jingoism

indicators.note: involved in means caught up inside, so the letters lie within the next words

parts.note: inside the words Balkan jingoism

explanation.surface: Outsiders play a part in nationalist fervour in south-east Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Kanji are the Chinese-derived characters used in Japanese writing, so they are foreign characters.

clue.text: Delay backing leading group with theory for the production of electricity

definitions.note: names the process; galvanism is electricity so produced

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a lag is a delay
the van is the leading group of an army or movement
an ism is a doctrine or theory

explanation.surface: A delay holds back the pioneers working on a theory of how to generate power.
explanation.definitionFit: Galvanism is electricity produced by chemical action, named after the Italian scientist Luigi Galvani.

clue.text: Peter Andre denoted voice as "Out of danger"

indicators.note: read as de-noted, it means a musical note is taken away from the word before it

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
taken as written; re is a note of the sol-fa scale
to voice is to sound

explanation.surface: The pop singer Peter Andre is said to have a voice that is 'Out of danger'.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Andre is a pop singer, but the two names are split: peter is a safe in safecracker's slang, and Andre loses its RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Safe and sound is an idiom for unharmed and secure, which means out of danger.
